newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese woman wounded in Israeli air raid.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese woman wounded in Israeli air raid.

text.p: Israeli planes attacked suspected Hizbollah targets in the Syrian-controlled eastern Bekaa Valley on Tuesday, security sources said.
Two jets fired four rockets into a mountainous area southwest of the town of Mashghara, just north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, they said.
A woman in the nearby village of Ain al-Tineh was wounded when a shrapnel hit her in the leg during the air attack -- Israel's 26th against Lebanon this year, the sources added.

Shortly after the air raid, pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) issued a statement saying its guerrillas attacked with machinguns and rocket-propelled grenades a motorised patrol belonging to the pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia in Toumat Niha, west of the area hit by the Israeli planes.
"The attack led to definite casualties among the members of the patrol," the statement said.
It added that another group simultaneously fired mortar bombs into the SLA outpost of Toumat Niha, just inside the occupation zone.
Pro-Israeli militia sources inside the zone said no one was injured in either attacks.
Hizbollah guerrillas frequently attack Israeli troops in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine-mile) -wide occupation zone in the south.
Earlier on Tuesday, two Lebanese civilians were killed and two were wounded in a roadside bomb explosion east of the south Lebanon market place of Nabatiyeh.
